audit.whatIsWrong: The page describes Spirit Cleave (W) as a stacking cleave that heals him — 'before his W cleave stacks', 'his sustain through W heal', 'stack his W spirit-cleave to third tier'. It also calls Soul Unbound an untargetable disengage.
audit.why: Riot's text: Spirit Cleave cleaves in a cone and grants Yone a shield scaled by champions hit, on a 14s cooldown that shortens with attack speed. There are no stacks and no tiers. Soul Unbound sends his spirit out and forces it back to the body he left behind — it is a repositioning tool, not untargetability.
audit.corrected: Every reference rebuilt on the shield, the 14s cooldown, and the snap-back-to-body mechanic.
sources: brief enemyKit W text + shield flag, cd 14
packet defects (never names any of Yone's abilities)

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers hand Lucian Level 1, Level 6, and 2+ items at 8/10, while whys[0] says 'you both have weak level 1s', whys[4] says his all-in beats yours at 6, and late says the matchup is 'lost on even footing'.
audit.why: Yone's Level 6 Fate Sealed pulls Lucian out of position and chains the second Mortal Steel knock-up; from first item onward his crit scaling closes the range Lucian's W move-speed holds open. Lucian's real ownership is Levels 2-3.
audit.corrected: Level 1 set to Skill; Level 6, First item and 2+ items flipped to Yone in both layers with matching ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why and phases[5].why describe The Culling and Lucian's first item as the spikes for stages that in fact belong to Yone.
audit.why: The level-6 shift is Fate Sealed plus the empowered Mortal Steel, and the first-item shift is his crit closing the gap — not Lucian's ult.
audit.corrected: Both lines rewritten to the real spike owner.
sources: brief enemyKit Q and R text

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing told you to break the Spirit Cleave shield before committing.
audit.why: The shield lands in front of exactly the burst string Lucian opens with and refreshes every 14 seconds — faster as he buys attack speed — so the first shot in a commit is a shield-breaker.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d now names Spirit Cleave and its cooldown.
sources: brief enemyKit W text and cd

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are the only part of this lane you reliably own. Your long auto range plus Lightslinger double-tap out-trades Yone before his W spirit-cleave has stacks, so weave Q-into-double-shot and Ardent Blaze the instant he steps to last-hit. Bait out his Q dash on minions — when it's down he has no gap-closer except E, and if you make him E to escape your trade he's defenseless for several seconds. Do NOT trade after he's landed his second Q dash (the empowered one); that's his burst, not yours.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the only part of this lane you reliably own. Your long auto range plus Lightslinger double-tap out-trades Yone before Spirit Cleave's shield is worth casting, so weave Q-into-double-shot and Ardent Blaze the instant he steps to last-hit. Mortal Steel only dashes on its second stack — bait that stack out on minions and he has no gap-closer for four seconds. Do NOT trade into the empowered second cast; the knock-up is his burst, not yours.

edits.before: Your edge is already thinning here. Levels 4-5 you can still kite his Q with W move-speed if you don't let him stack W cleave on you, but mana gets tight and his sustain through W heal closes the gap. At 6 the lane flips: his R knockup over the wave plus the empowered second Q means his all-in now beats yours unless your E dash is up to get out. Treat 6 as "respect, don't contest" — only commit when you've baited his E rewind first.
edits.after: Your edge is already thinning here. Levels 4-5 you can still kite Mortal Steel with W move-speed, but mana gets tight and the Spirit Cleave shield eats a poke every 14 seconds. At 6 the lane flips: Fate Sealed pulls you through the wave and the empowered second Mortal Steel knocks up, so his all-in beats yours unless your E is up. Treat 6 as respect, not contest — commit only once Soul Unbound is spent.

edits.before: This is lost on even footing — Yone is exactly the mobile, untargetable-disengage scaler that wrecks you. His E spirit-rewind snaps him out of your Culling channel and back to safety, wasting your R entirely, and his two-form crit burst out-duels your squishy frame once he itemizes. Your only path is the lead you built at levels 2-6: if you didn't snowball, play for objectives and let your team handle him, because the straight 1v1 only gets worse from here.
edits.after: This is lost on even footing — Yone is exactly the mobile crit scaler that wrecks you. Soul Unbound sends his spirit out and forces it back to the body he parked in safety, so a Culling spent on the spirit buys you nothing, and his crit burst out-duels your frame once he itemizes. Your only path is the lead you built at levels 2-6: if you didn't snowball, play objectives and let your team handle him.

edits.before: Win the level 2-3 window with Q-W-E double-shots before his W cleave stacks up
edits.after: Win the level 2-3 window with Q-W-E double-shots before Spirit Cleave is worth casting

edits.before: Stack his W spirit-cleave to third tier and trade through your kite
edits.after: Shield with Spirit Cleave every 14s and trade straight through your kite

notes: Riot's Spirit Cleave text in the kit file describes a shield only, with no healing and no stack mechanic, so I wrote the shield and dropped the invented 'third tier'. Whether Soul Unbound's spirit can be damaged or targeted while the body stands elsewhere is not stated in the kit text, so the page now says only that the spirit is forced back to the body — no untargetability claim in either direction. Fate Sealed's pull as a knock-up chain from Mortal Steel is inferred from both ability texts and is worth a second look if a Yone specialist reviews this page.
